svg.text: Components are the units of deployment: the smallest entities deployable as part of a system (Java jar, Ruby gem, .NET DLL; aggregations of binaries or, in interpreted
languages, source files); well-designed ones stay independently deployable and so independently developable
Early years
programmers fix load addresses (origin *200); libraries
kept as source
Library binary
compile the library apart, load at a known address
(2000 octal); app must fit 0000 to 1777
Split apps
apps outgrew the gap, so split in two address segments
around the library; fragmentation
Relocatable binaries
a smart loader places code anywhere using flags; names
emitted as external references and definitions: the
linking loader
Linkers
linking too slow (tape, disks, hundreds of libraries,
over an hour); split into a separate linker producing a
quickly loadable file
C: .c to .o to executable; turnaround again an hour or
more: Murphy's law of program size
Moore beat Murphy by the mid-1990s: faster disks, cheap RAM and clocks from 1 MHz to 100 MHz cut link time to seconds, so linking at load time became feasible:
Active-X, shared libraries, .jar files and the component plugin architecture.
